clean_body: Do not share this: A private plea | | | | | | Peter, I just returned home from a week of agonizing meetings with Republican leadership, and I honestly have nowhere else to turn but to you. The things I heard in DC and back here in the state are too difficult to share publicly, but I wrote a special, private note for you— and for you only —detailing the crushing reality. The liberals are pouring millions into their campaigns, and I'm losing sleep knowing that if we fail to hold our seats, we fail President Trump. I'm not supposed to tell you how bad the deficit is, but I can't look away from the truth. Please, I'm humbling myself before you, asking you to read my confidential note immediately. You are my only hope to fight back against this tidal wave of liberal money. And please, promise me you won't share this. If this note gets out, President Trump's fight is over. Forever Humbled, I didn’t run for Senate to sit quietly on the sidelines. I’m a mom, a conservative, and a proud Alabamian—and I came to fight for the values that make America strong. Faith. Family. Freedom. The Left is doing everything they can to tear it all down. But I didn’t come to Washington to play games. I came to fight for the people who feel forgotten, overlooked, and ignored. From securing the border to protecting our kids and defending our way of life—I’m in this for the long haul. This fight isn’t easy, but it’s worth it. And I’m not going anywhere. Will you stand with me? Paid for by Britt for Alabama, Inc.

name: Pramila Jayapal
subject: Wealth inequality is a policy choice
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Pramila for Congress
body:
After the SpaceX IPO, Elon Musk is now worth over $1.1 trillion.
# [](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/892?refcode=em20260612-6348-footer&t=1&akid=6348%2E420207%2E3OTpmZ)
Peter,
**Elon Musk just became the world’s first _trillionaire_**. After the SpaceX IPO, he’s now worth over $1.1 trillion.
$1.1 TRILLION. It's a number so staggering that our brains aren't wired to intuitively understand it.
And it’s happening at a time when 76% of Americans say the cost of living is their biggest economic concern, with 65% saying a middle-class lifestyle is out of reach and 77% saying it’s harder to achieve than a decade ago.
In 49 states, the average renter’s wage isn’t enough to afford a two-bedroom apartment. In 37 states, it’s not even enough for a one-bedroom.
And as of this spring, inflation has outpaced wage growth over the previous 12 months — **meaning workers’ paychecks actually are losing ground.**
Meanwhile, one man is accumulating wealth faster than any human being in the history of the world. And it isn’t an accident.
**It’s a policy choice made by politicians who are more interested in protecting billionaires than fighting for working people.**
They implement policies that let the ultra-wealthy pay lower tax rates than nurses and teachers, creating a rigged system that funnels more and more to the top while the rest of us fall further behind.
**I refuse to accept this.** It’s why I’ve been pushing for policies like a wealth tax, a federal living wage, and Medicare for All—because working people deserve more than scraps.
But Peter, I’m going to be honest with you.
The forces standing in the way of a progressive agenda that puts working people first are powerful. The same billionaires (and now a trillionaire) who are getting richer by the minute are spending huge sums of money to prop up Trump and his MAGA allies, and take down progressive voices in Congress who dare to fight back.
That means I’m going to need your help to take them on. I don’t take money from corporate PACs or lobbyists, and I don’t have billionaires on speed dial. My average online contribution this year is just $27.16.
[**So I’m asking you directly: Will you chip in $27.16 today to help me keep building this people-powered movement and fight for an economy that works for ALL of us, not just those at the top?**](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/53804?c0=pj-em-20260612.W3hRtZ&refcode=em20260612-6348&t=2&akid=6348%2E420207%2E3OTpmZ)

In solidarity,
Pramila Jayapal

name: AOC
subject: Our responsibility is to take care of people.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez for Congress
body:
#
Our responsibility in Congress is to take care of people.
So before we spend billions of dollars building data centers across the country, **we need to meet some basic protections for people**.
We need some guarantees on our water, and the air we breathe.
We need to make sure that there's a plan for the jobs that stand to be wiped out, so we're not leaving people out to dry.
We should be starting congressional investigations into the effects of AI data centers, and figuring out — with precision — how we protect our water supplies, our power bills, and keep people from getting sick.
The AI lobby has spent billions to become part of our daily lives. [Take a moment to fill out our brief survey about AI today.](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/survey/2026-ai-data-center-moratorium-survey-2/?source=em20260612-11693-P_FND_EGR_GRM&t=3&akid=11693%2E2526796%2EKfUFGA)
**[Take the survey now →](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/survey/2026-ai-data-center-moratorium-survey-2/?source=em20260612-11693-P_FND_EGR_GRM&t=4&akid=11693%2E2526796%2EKfUFGA)**
I know as a politician these companies are going to spend a billion dollars against me for saying it, but **politicians — especially Democrats — should pledge not to take AI money**. 🤷🏻♀️
I refuse all corporate lobbyist money and I don’t believe we should be bankrolled by special interests at all. Each cycle the big dark money interests rotate - NRA, AIPAC, fossil fuel lobby, etc. **This cycle it’s the AI lobby**.
[Help us continue the fight by making a grassroots contribution today.](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/37587?refcode=em20260612-11693-P_FND_EGR_GRM&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=5&akid=11693%2E2526796%2EKfUFGA)
**[Contribute](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/37587?refcode=em20260612-11693-P_FND_EGR_GRM&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=6&akid=11693%2E2526796%2EKfUFGA)**
In solidarity,
Alexandria

**TODAY'S TOP STORIES**
**[The election analyst Newt Gingrich trusts has a word for 2020, and it isn’t “stolen”](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY JEN SCHUMANN, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
Stolen is the wrong word.
Seth Keshel says so himself. And Keshel is a retired Army intelligence captain who has spent nearly six years tagged in headlines as an election denier and a conspiracy theorist. Ask him the obvious question—was the 2020 election stolen—and he says no. He says something else.
“I don’t believe the elections are stolen. I believe that they’re rigged,” Keshel said. “And that’s what Newt Gingrich believes too.”
Keshel, a former Army captain of military intelligence and Afghanistan veteran, built a second career reading election returns the way he once read a battlefield.

**[Eleven Colorado lawmakers on the ballot first reached office through appointment](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY JEN SCHUMANN, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* **Vacancy committees, not voters, decided who represents these districts:** one lawmaker, Jamie Jackson, was appointed to a House seat with just 10 votes from a 19-member committee, while a 2024 Colorado Politics analysis found nearly a third of the entire 100-seat legislature first arrived via appointment rather than election.
* **Some vacancies were created by lawmakers cashing in or stepping away shortly after winning reelection:** Chris Hansen resigned just nine weeks after voters returned him to the Senate to take a $500,000 utility job, and Janet Buckner left weeks after a 45,000-vote win, with replacements chosen by committee votes of 61-37 and 35-of-42 respectively.
* **Even when committees fumble the process, voters rarely get the final say:** one Senate seat was filled by Gov. Polis himself after a vacancy committee missed its paperwork deadline, and historically appointees have lost a primary challenge only a handful of times in 25 years — though five of these 11 face opponents on the June 30 ballot.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**

By the time he walked out, Lorenzo Sewell had given his life to Christ. That same day he went to his drug boss and quit._

Now they’re holding their fourth summit, and this year’s program includes discussions on geothermal energy, data centers, critical minerals, electric cooperative power supplies, workforce development and Colorado River issues._
**[Colorado grew on a wave. The wave is gone.](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** **BY SHAINA COLE | STATE | JUNE 9** _Colorado crossed six million people in 2025, according to the U.S. Census Bureau. _You're getting this message because you’ve supported good causes and Democratic candidates. We need your support to continue fighting for our democracy. We love having you in our network, but if you only want our most important email updates,[click here.](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/108?t=2&akid=2474%2E259176%2EdE-6zV) If you'd like to unsubscribe, [click here.](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/109?t=3&akid=2474%2E259176%2EdE-6zV)_

[](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/11115?source=LOC_EM_FR_2026.06.12_Sand-Gut_B5_F1_S1_C1_90AC-365DON_N-T1&t=4&akid=2474%2E259176%2EdE-6zV) Politicians famously lie a lot, Peter. Now I love a good practical joke here and there, but I don’t lie. That’s one of the many reasons I consider myself a public servant, NOT a politician. So I want to give you the full, unvarnished truth of how I’m feeling about chances in the toss-up race for Governor of Iowa. **Hang on before I start yapping:** I just got my official opponent, and get this: he’s a Kansan culture warrior backed by _Steve King._ **Game on.** Now that we’re up against Zach Lahn and the partisan machine behind him, **[_will you rush a donation between my campaign and Blue Amp Action to help us maximize the post-primary energy here in Iowa? Every bit counts in a race THIS competitive._](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/11115?source=LOC_EM_FR_2026.06.12_Sand-Gut_B5_F1_S1_C1_90AC-365DON_N-T1&t=5&akid=2474%2E259176%2EdE-6zV)** | [Split a Donation >>](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/11115?source=LOC_EM_FR_2026.06.12_Sand-Gut_B5_F1_S1_C1_90AC-365DON_N-T1&t=6&akid=2474%2E259176%2EdE-6zV)
---
Honestly, the primary results didn’t change my feelings much at all. **My gut and recent polling tell me we have a slight lead, but this governor’s race will probably come down to no more than 10,000 votes.**
I don’t want you to think I’m not confident in our chances. I’m extremely confident, in fact: experts have this race pinned as a toss-up, we have a big tent filled with Iowans from literally every walk of life, we have a provably persuasive message, we’re running several TV ads with great feedback from voters, the list goes on and on.

We are witnessing a cascade of primaries in _Iowa_ , _California_ , _South Carolina_ ...and _**right around the corner, here in Arizona**_. _Early in-person voting will begin and mail-in ballots will be accepted starting June 24_. You and all good Republicans in LD27 will be entrusted with selecting a nominee for state senate who best encapsulates our party and puts the best foot forward for our platform. _**For over a decade, I’ve been a party stalwart in Phoenix, working with the Republican majority to pass good, common sense legislation and doing battle with Katie Hobbs and her cronies**_. More than anyone in Arizona, I have spearheaded the movement for election integrity, ensuring that our vote counting is quick, secure, and transparent. **Since he first announced for president in 2015** and promised to build a wall on our southern border, **I have stood side by side with Donald Trump and his efforts to Make America Great Again**. **I was a co-founder of the Arizona Freedom Caucus** , because I know that the Republican Party means nothing if it does not champion proven conservative solutions and uphold the Constitution of our Founding Fathers. I am a faithful Christian, a patriotic American, and a dutiful Republican, in that order. [**It’s not too late to make a difference for our party: chip in $20 for my state senate campaign**](https://us.list-manage.com/BndmSfqIFV_?e=b78dc6f299&c2id=0224aa72dff2928514ac0b5416ed4e8b), and be ready to cast your vote for Anthony Kern once ballots drop on June 24. ## US, Iran Agree on Peace Deal Text
The U.S. and Iran have reached a [final peace deal text](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0D1u6zAQBODTUB0Naknrp2DxGnV-bUphLa6sTShSIDd2fPvAKXKB1APM4Ju3y3xBjpxu_3EnL2ueEz1qJBEqMxdMeCtEOyV55BJDXblUkRkMdNp0urVzQI7P2TXBr0RAtiHf9kNr3dm2XbP50Y3Dch2uIzobegfOLWEMyzAOeCVCbNi_2kzX2taYwbpT55YODazW9TZgH5QzFFhyOb1nTrLRGp_5TuW05L2JfhM5qrL_FEwKJtlo4xhfmYLpyJGXp4KJk1BJKJwTRgXTeQQw5qwP_OAqmPRn1S-uPggX0oEwaqEv0b9-BVNTfDgeHCPXrlfO3Hbkn6VG_nTd3cN3AAAA__9nh4RU), the strongest signal yet that the war may be ending, Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif announced Friday. A senior Trump administration official said the [agreement could be signed](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLFutDAQhJ_GdCDb67PvChd_Q3d_mxIZvMAmxiB7c-jePiKvkGaakb7RfB_P4RkoUV7-hw09z_uQ8awJmbEMVEIOS0HcMPO5lxTrTKUyD1pq20rbKhhioPQeTBP9jKgRGvTK3RWYGyjbrH6CUVpzG60E91DjXU7moR2Cs4CIEBryF01aBUrKO5jOmskGqWcwDmJwURiJkXgv3edOmVec03t_YemmfWuSX5mPKuCf0L3Q_Xme3ZTH6SqF7i-00L28Qmmh--tTGzGklsv3drRH-KLKIbd1DYXmbuUtNcXH46SUqFonjFy2QOl3jf-k6OX1TwAAAP__hfR5YA) within days, though Iran's foreign ministry cautioned that Tehran hasn't reached "a final conclusion." U.S. officials pushed back on information that has been shared publicly by Iran's media about the contents of the forthcoming deal. President Trump wrote in an angry [Truth Social post](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0Dtu6zAQheHVkJ0NPoakbsHiAoE6pwqQUpiII4sBJQrk2IZ3HzhbSHsO8BX_52W6YC55v77jRpGXOu306IWYqU254Y7XRrTRzo_aSupLbp15Msr4k_InbaeEuTwnkCkuRIaspKjDoC04q71cowuJHNLwtYBWs4c5ofPaqETgXfg3yxxfmvLaaqUGC2cPs0dlFgvBJgxJgKKUubbzd807r7SUZ71TO891kyWuzEcX9r8wozAjtxuvvc4Zy-t_jaAaYXmrO5b00W7bIcx41M5dmFFrH2wAPVgHTlkVQLaYjkcuJXcfBKjrhvmXkvynPvdofgIAAP__r8l32Q) Friday morning that the public reporting about the deal has "NOTHING to do with the terms that were agreed to, in writing." Unconfirmed reports say the memorandum would extend the ceasefire for 60 days, reopen the Strait of Hormuz, and tie sanctions relief to Iranian compliance. Hours earlier, U.S. forces reportedly [shot down two Iranian drones](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0L2O6yAUBOCnwR0WfxcnBcVt3GXbLa0TOCSssLHgxChvv_IW-wJbjzSjbz5vyw1STtvjA1Z0FMuyYW8ZibAuqcIGj4q44ka91BxaTLURLUooy4XlUi8BUn4vZgguIirUAzo5XaQ2_7S0w9PZK4ZolfFeeLQSpmi01Qj366QuAcOQ3NkmrNRSiIs2ozXeglBRm0kHmAIzAkOiUsevkjZ6YszvcmAdfVmH7J5Ee2P6P1MzU3PvffT3dirOnKk5pwP5aw9A2JiaTxTvUPmrcaqvdec7gkceEDL_1TI1D9WFvaecU7MTM-KxQso_m_Snow6nvgMAAP__3O9-5A) targeting commercial ships in the strait.
## Soaring IPO Makes Elon Musk a Trillionaire
SpaceX broke every record in its [Friday market debut](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2uozAQhZ8GOpB_BpsULrahy7ZbosEMyWyMjWxv2Lz9FfcVbnekI52j7_tzn-_IgePjN-7k6pbmSGcJVCvlmTNGfGSinWI9Uw5r2TiXWmcllOmE6aSeV-TwmaFd3UakSLfkpB2lhkFL0z7dCGBhhHG8LXaQNxgsDsIsktDD4hFadteaMFJLIUYNvQFvUKhNg9Ur2rUBQSvXlPu_iWN90hY-6U2592lvg3vWepRG_2rU1KjpPM8-Lv6iuPpGTcu_wpFKadS0Y35RvVI50NP_jo_UlZr8qzsye-qyj6jhZo1os1uPk0PgYmwD4rEjh-_H-iNNb6e-AgAA__9-7Xx7), capping the biggest IPO in history and making Elon Musk the world's first trillionaire. The rocket and AI company raised roughly $75 billion at $135 per share, nearly three times more than any company in history. The stock opened at $150 under the ticker SPCX and climbed past $169, pushing the company's valuation above $2 trillion. Musk, who owns about 42% of SpaceX and controls roughly 85% of its voting power, saw his [net worth top](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkD1y6yAURlcDnTz8CdkFxWvU-bUpNQQu0k0QaODGjnefUbaQ8jvfzCnO2325e8xY1v9-B0epLgWePQMRtAWbL35tADsUetaWY0_YOtGihLKDsIPUS_SYX4vh0SUABZqDk9NVajNqafnmvBeQwhjSKG83AZMQNlk5BRvGdxlG4OhOm7BSSyGu2lysCdYLlbSZdPRTZEZARKrt8lGx0AYpv-oD2iXUnWe3ER2d6X9MzUzNtMGGOZ8fU_NRM4bXiSFspea6nmO8KXm1aoBcy7B_9c-hHz7A90ANc8ZaPDZgaubNxeN5om4nZsS6e_w1c_pTqodTPwEAAP__DFd-VA) an estimated $1.1 trillion. Around 4,400 current and former employees also stand to become millionaires.
## U.S. Soccer Team Scores Opening World Cup Win
The U.S. Men's Soccer Team opened its first World Cup game [with a 4-1 victory](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGu4yAURL8Gd7bgQsAuKLZxl223tIi5JKwwWHATlL9_Sn7hdSONNJpz_l23q4sp5vtfd6ClULaMvSUkwrrF6rK7V8QDM_VSk28h1ka0AQc9cj0KuXkX03tTg7cBEVAOaIWZhVQXKfTwsEIZkLeg-O0G84woxIyLvOCsF8MX7oZoP2tcCyk4n6WatNq14xCkMtI745ni6COVOv0vMdMDQ3qXF9ZpL8eQ7IPobEz-YbAyWHvvE7Yzf0oGayv7jvUTqNQ3g3VjsEbPYFULV9qYmcH6bEemNn4Jx_15juXEjHXsro0n1oA7DdX6s8eUYtOGKX4_XEzfA_Qray8LPwEAAP___6OAag) over Paraguay in front of a roaring American crowd in Los Angeles. The Americans [struck first](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0DFywyAQheHToM6ehUUgFRRp1DkpUiQdg8TKJoOEBzZ2fPuMc4V0b17xFf_HyZ9Cymk_v4aNHK_F73RvmZip-lTDHs6VaKOd76Xm2NZUG7NXoMwBzEGijyHlh9dddCuRIuzISTtI1D1K012cHvpxwR5nM_fzOGM_aNAxhCUosDMMXXJPDYxECTCgPhq9mABqRW0xBhuFBoqJSz1-lbTzhdb8KDeqx6VsXXYX5msT-CLUJNT083yFmqa3z_drqdyEmhoH_n4OBaY3oOxopbWjtHrArrp4vaecUzNWaDhvIeU_mf-V4-bUbwAAAP__AXxwxw) in the seventh minute when a Christian Pulisic and Weston McKennie move forced Paraguay's Damian Bobadilla to turn the ball into his own net. American forward Folarin Balogun then took over, scoring twice as the U.S. built a 3-0 first-half lead.

Balogun [completed his brace](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFuwyAQxvGnwVsi7sBgDwxdvKUdOrSbdQrnhAqbCK5J8_aV-wrdPn3Db_h_nOYTpZy2yyutHGQp88aPllmE65wqbXSpzCtv8ig1x7ak2kRm1OgO2h3AzJFSfs62i2FhRjYdB_ADGNsbcN01APLY4wimjzwCINKZaBh1HMl6tEOXwq5pBwa0How9Ont2pHEx1ptIPiqrOSYp9fhV0iZXXvKz3Lkez2XtcriK3JoyLwonhdPP_iqcprfP91up0hROTUi-94Ha9Q6M9c73ztkBNHQ1xNsj5Zya88rqy0op_8nyrxz3gL8BAAD__6yScGE) in first-half stoppage time, the first World Cup brace by a U.S. player since the inaugural tournament in 1930.

The U.S. faces Australia next [on June 19](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0L1y6yAQQOGnQZ01_Bl0C4rbqHPalBrMLtYmSHhgbY3fPpPkEdKf-YrzflkukQrtt7e4YeBclx2PXpAZ20It7vHWEDfc-aitQM_UOvOipXYn6U7KLBCpvBY7QMiIGs2AQflJGXs2yg1rAC19Ngkg-xSvk0Ow_7zy1-l89gYnN1D41qRTRkk5GTs6m1yUOhvrDUQPwkoE4trGj0o7r5jLqz6xjaluQwkr870L81_oWej5OI7x0XtN6TcQeu5pRXgUPDGlT-Qu9Pzo285DC3A_qBTqzgsrb1uk8oPyn048g_4KAAD__wzBc8w) in Seattle.

| | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18] | | | | | | Do you have money in any of these banks? Maine Democrat Senate nominee Graham Platner has come under heavy fire for his many immoral and vile statements. These include lying about a Nazi tattoo, justifying rape, denigrating American hero Chris Kyle, and making remarks about me. I'm the soldier in the viral combat video whom Platner stated "didn't deserve to live."
Platner and his supporters always fall back on the excuse that Platner suffers from PTSD. Many Americans suffer from PTSD, myself included. The issue isn't PTSD; we should be blaming his elitist background.
Due to Platner's privileged upbringing, I seriously doubt he had to truly face any consequences for his abhorrent behavior. We all know a Graham Platner in our lives. He is the "Do you know who my daddy is?" "I can do whatever I want" type of guy.
Platner's family sent him to elite schools and, as an adult, financed vacations and trips to Europe. His father gave him $200,000 for his house, and his mother is his oyster farming client. They have extended a large safety net, essentially not letting him fail in life or learn the lessons associated with struggle. He has lacked many of the character-building experiences associated with enduring the hardships of life and the struggles that working-class Americans endure on a daily basis.
Graham Platner's behavior is not based upon his diagnosis of PTSD but rather on being coddled in socialite society, where accountability is non-existent. Platner has never experienced the rigors of raising children, providing for a family, stressing about bills, or doing what it takes to be a true man. He has continued to act like an entitled child and shirk any responsibility because he has always had his socialite and elitist family to fall back on.
He has tried to cosplay as part of blue-collar America despite his privileged upbringing. The worlds have clashed, and now America wants accountability, not excuses and not a scapegoat. The finger-pointing toward PTSD is unacceptable. It is a victimhood response and, again, is being used as a blanket excuse for poor character.
Due to the numerous controversies involving Platner, many appear to have occurred online, from his Reddit posts to years spent trolling on an app that has become notorious for attracting adult sexual predators seeking contact with minors.
Yet he calls himself a working man. Working men normally don't have the time, desire, or low character to engage in those behaviors.
I am a combat-wounded veteran, Purple Heart recipient, and come from a blue-collar working-class family. I've failed and struggled numerous times in life. Not once did I ever use PTSD as a scapegoat. It's an insult to everyone who has PTSD: veterans, first responders, sexual assault survivors, and many others.
Like the majority of Americans, I have faced life--a hard life and a life that builds and tests character. Struggle builds character, and Graham Platner and his "Do you know who my daddy is?" upbringing have shielded him from that struggle.
Ask yourself a simple question. Would you want Graham Platner alone with your children? Would you want him alone with your wife? Would you want a man like Graham Platner dating your daughter?
Let's just call it what it is. As a combat veteran who has openly struggled with PTSD myself, this isn't PTSD. This is about a total lack of character. Call it that. Not PTSD, but rather a lack of character and accountability.
Teddy Daniels
**Teddy Daniels is a decorated U.S. Army combat veteran.**
